authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve the authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window, or publication status.
sourcePolicy: MNRE's official scheme page, comprehensive guidelines, national PM-KUSUM portal and official state implementing routes are the primary sources. Component A, B, C individual pump solarisation and C feeder-level solarisation remain separate routes. UdyamVeda explains and prepares evidence but does not file state applications, handle OTPs or represent itself as an implementing agency.

records.sourceAnchor: Three components, capacity/assistance parameters, designated State route and national period through 31 March 2026
observations: The official MNRE page describes Component A for 500 kW to 2 MW decentralized renewable plants, Component B for standalone agricultural pumps up to 7.5 HP, and Component C for individual pump and feeder-level solarisation.

The page states central financial assistance of 30% for general regions and 50% for specified special regions for applicable pump/solarisation routes, calculated against the lower of benchmark or tender cost; State support and beneficiary/finance balance remain separate buckets.

Component A, pump installation, individual pump solarisation and feeder-level solarisation have different beneficiaries, implementing agencies, land/pump/capacity conditions, procurement routes and payment mechanics; they must not be presented as one generic subsidy.

The MNRE page states the scheme period through 31 March 2026, while the national portal reports achievements as of 31 July 2026. The later reporting does not by itself establish a new universal national application window or continuation.

State allocation and designated State/DISCOM implementing routes control actionable applications. A business or farmer must not be told that the national record alone proves current local availability.
reviewFollowUps: Reconcile any official extension, continuation or state-specific current window after 31 March 2026 before surfacing an actionable recommendation.
Confirm the selected component, beneficiary/entity class, land or pump condition, capacity/HP, State allocation, vendor and designated implementing agency.
Verify current State/DISCOM application forms, deadlines, beneficiary contribution, bank-finance route, benchmark/tender cost and completion conditions.
Keep central assistance, State subsidy, loan finance, feed-in tariff and any DISCOM incentive in separate benefit buckets.
Check amendments, vendor lists, portal notices, grievance routes and obtain a human reviewer decision; no national record should publish as active until the continuation/window issue is resolved.

publicationGuard.reason: Official MNRE sources confirm the component structure and financial-assistance framework, but the national period ended on 31 March 2026 on the cited scheme page and no universal post-period continuation was established. State implementation, current allocation, vendor route, component-specific terms and reviewer decision remain unresolved.
